lesson.title: What Immutability Actually Promises
lesson.summary: A tuple can never have an element reassigned or removed, the same guarantee strings already gave you, but that promise covers only the tuple's own slots, not any mutable object sitting inside it.
lesson.body:
You met this same idea already with String Immutability: once a string exists, you cannot change one of its characters in place, you can only build a new string. Tuples make the identical promise about their elements. Once a tuple is created, you cannot reassign, insert, or delete any of the slots it holds. Trying to do so does not silently fail; Python raises an error immediately.

coordinates = (10, 20)

try:
    coordinates[0] = 99
except TypeError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

This prints Error: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment. That message is Python being explicit about the guarantee: tuples simply do not offer a way to change what is stored at a given position, unlike lists.

The subtlety worth sitting with is that immutability applies to the tuple's own slots, the references it holds, not to whatever object each of those references points to. If one of those objects happens to be mutable, like a list, that object can still change, and the tuple will not stop it, because the tuple itself has not been touched at all; it is still holding a reference to the exact same list it always was.

nested = (1, [2, 3])
nested[1].append(4)
print(nested)

This prints (1, [2, 3, 4]). No error was raised, because nested[1] = something_else would have been forbidden, but nested[1].append(4) never reassigns slot 1 of the tuple; it reaches into the list already sitting there and modifies that list in place. The tuple still points to the same list object it did before, so the tuple itself was never changed. This distinction, between changing which object a slot refers to and changing the contents of that object, is exactly what "immutable" means for a tuple, and it is worth remembering before you assume a tuple guarantees its contents can never change at all.
